content:
marta.ops: Heads up — our us-west-2 canary batch of kernel upgrades to 6.3.0 just started failing to bring GPUs up. About ~30 hosts stuck at early boot with nvidia modules missing, pods OOMing or evicted.

ian-infra: Confirmed. Saw same in us-west-2-a. dmesg shows: 
```
modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/6.3.0-123-generic
kernel: nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout
```
DKMS logs indicate builds only for 5.15 kernels.

lucas-eng: Which driver version are those AMIs using? We shipped 535.x prebuilts for 5.15 but not for 6.x. If DKMS wasn't invoked at firstboot the modules won't exist for 6.x kernels.

sree: Most affected hosts are our custom AMI (ami-gpu-2025-03) with packaged driver 535.35.12 and a DKMS recipe that expects older kernel headers. Example from journalctl: 
```
Dec 10 03:12:45 host kernel: nvidia_drm: probe of nvidia-drm failed with error -22
Dec 10 03:12:46 host modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia-uvm not found in directory /lib/modules/6.3.0-123-generic
```

ops-bot: kernel-roller: Canary batch 1 (us-west-2) deployed at 1767212300.

natalie: Recommendation — pause the rollout immediately and mark the canary ASG as unschedulable. Drain affected nodes with fast-evict so control-plane jobs can reschedule. Also prepare a mitigation plan for capacity loss (cross-region spill or burst). :exclamation:

ian-infra: Agreed. Pausing rollout. Short-term options: 1) revert nodes to 5.15 AMI snapshot; 2) push a prebuilt driver package containing 6.x modules; 3) ensure DKMS runs at early boot and has matching kernel-headers. Rebuild AMI probably fastest for fleet stability.

marta.ops: Cost/impact note — ~120 GPUs across the zone flagged unhealthy; if we shift to other regions we'll incur egress and spot premium. Estimate addl cost ~8-12% for next 48hrs if we failover. We're throttling new scheduled jobs to limit retries.

lucas-eng: If we bring up temporary capacity in us-east-1 with 5.15 AMI we can pick up queued jobs, but distributed training perf will be worse (NCCL P2P over WAN). Also some jobs assume intra-region NVLINK — not possible.

alex-sre: Seeing NCCL WARNs correlated with the hosts losing GPUs: "NCCL WARN Call to send failed" and downstream hangs in Horovod. Opened incident INC-1234.

sree: Proposed immediate plan: 
1) Pause kernel rollout (done).
2) Roll back canary ASG nodes to previous AMI (5.15) for affected hosts to restore capacity.
3) In parallel, produce a new AMI with kernel-headers+prebuilt 535.* modules for 6.3 and smoke test in CI.
4) Add DKMS CI job that attempts building against 6.x headers and reports failures.
5) Once we have prebuilts and DKMS CI green, resume a much smaller canary.

marta.ops: Owners: ian-infra -> AMI rollback + revert plan, lucas-eng -> driver AMI build & CI, natalie -> capacity orchestration & cost estimate, alex-sre -> incident coordination and job rescheduling guidance. I'll spin up a follow-up postmortem thread after stabilizing nodes.

deploy-bot: kernel-roller: rollout paused by marta.ops at 1767212400 :white_check_mark:

ian-infra: Quick notes for postmortem — check kernel-headers packaging step in our AMI pipeline, confirm DKMS hook runs on firstboot for all instance types, and consider shipping prebuilt modules for major kernel families we intend to roll.

marta.ops: Thanks — please add any logs to INC-1234 and tag the AMI PRs. We need timeline estimate for AMI rebuild (lucas?) and cost for spill (natalie).

lucas-eng: I'll try to get a prebuilt AMI + smoke test out in 4-6 hours, will post links in the incident.

natalie: I'll model the cost and open a capacity shift plan. If we need spot burst in us-east-1 I'll coordinate with finance.

marta.ops: Closing the loop here for now — pausing rollout prevented wider outage. We'll reconvene once AMIs are ready. :thumbsup:
